## Linnet
Status: draft

Cold brew coffee is a smooth, low-acid alternative to traditional hot coffee, made by steeping coarse-ground beans in cold water for an extended period—typically 12 to 24 hours. The result is a concentrated, sweet-tasting brew that can be diluted with water or milk and served over ice. Unlike iced coffee, which is simply hot coffee cooled down, cold brew extracts flavors slowly without the bitterness that heat can bring out.

## Kittiwake
Status: draft

Choosing the right coffee beans is essential for a quality cold brew. Medium to coarse grinds work best—they allow water to extract flavor without over-extracting, which would introduce bitter notes. Many enthusiasts prefer single-origin beans with chocolatey or nutty flavor notes, though any high-quality, freshly roasted coffee will yield good results.
